name: Makita
description:
Makita is a Japanese power tool manufacturer founded in March 1915 as Makita Electric Works, an electric motor and equipment repair shop opened by Mosaburo Makita in Nagoya. The company incorporated in 1938, relocated to Anjō in Aichi Prefecture in 1945, and shifted decisively into power tools in 1958 when it began selling Japan's first domestically produced portable electric planer. By 1969 Makita led the Japanese power tool market, and it has since grown into one of the three or four most recognized cordless tool brands in the United States alongside DeWalt and Milwaukee.

## The 18V LXT battery platform

Makita's identity in the US is built almost entirely around its 18V LXT lithium-ion platform. LXT is the broadest single-voltage cordless lineup on the market, with well over 300 tools sharing one battery interface — drills, drivers, saws, grinders, outdoor power equipment, lighting, and a large range of jobsite gear. For a buyer, that breadth is the central reason to choose Makita: once you own LXT batteries, almost any tool you add slots into the same charger and pack ecosystem. Makita also sells an 18V X2 system that pairs two LXT batteries to deliver 36V-class power for saws and outdoor tools without forcing customers onto a separate battery standard, and a 40V max XGT platform aimed at the most demanding industrial and construction applications. The XGT line is deliberately kept separate from LXT — the two are not cross-compatible — so US buyers should decide up front which platform their fleet will live on.

## US pro versus DIY positioning

Makita sits closer to the professional end of the market than to the budget-DIY end. Its tools are common on remodeling, electrical, plumbing, cabinet, and finish-carpentry jobsites, where the priorities are balance, low weight, and all-day comfort rather than the highest possible torque numbers. Makita's cordless drills, for example, tend to be lighter and better balanced than the highest-torque competitors, which is a real advantage for installers working overhead or in confined spaces. The brand is also widely bought by serious homeowners who want professional-grade durability and the security of a huge battery ecosystem, even if they do not need it daily.

## What Makita is known for

Makita is best known for the breadth of its LXT ecosystem, for light and well-balanced ergonomics, for brushless motor efficiency across its current generation, and for kits that frequently ship with larger-capacity batteries than competitors bundle. Its rapid chargers are a recurring strength, often reaching full charge in around 30 minutes. The trade-off versus brands like Milwaukee is that Makita's flagship drills and drivers generally chase balance and weight over class-leading torque, and Makita's standard US power tool warranty is three years against the longer warranties some rivals offer.

## Who should choose Makita

Choose Makita if you value a light, comfortable tool and want access to the widest cordless lineup available, or if you are already invested in LXT batteries. It is an especially strong fit for trades that run tools all day and for homeowners who want one battery system to cover power tools and outdoor equipment alike. Buyers who need the absolute highest torque for heavy structural fastening, or who want the longest warranty for the lowest price, should compare Makita against Milwaukee and Bosch before committing.

faq.a: Makita is headquartered in Anjō, Aichi Prefecture, Japan, where the company has been based since relocating there in 1945. It was originally founded in Nagoya in 1915 as Makita Electric Works. Makita operates manufacturing plants worldwide, including in the United States, Germany, Brazil, and China.

faq.q: What is the Makita 18V LXT platform?
faq.a: LXT is Makita's 18V lithium-ion battery system, the broadest single-voltage cordless lineup on the market with over 300 compatible tools. Every LXT tool uses the same battery interface, so one pack and charger work across drills, saws, grinders, and outdoor equipment. It is the main reason buyers commit to the Makita ecosystem.

faq.q: Is Makita a professional or DIY brand?
faq.a: Makita is primarily a professional brand that is also popular with serious DIYers. Its tools are common on remodeling, electrical, and finish-carpentry jobsites, where light weight and balance matter more than maximum torque. Homeowners buy Makita for professional-grade durability and the security of a large battery ecosystem.

faq.q: Are Makita LXT and XGT batteries compatible?
faq.a: No, Makita's 18V LXT and 40V max XGT platforms are not cross-compatible — they use different battery interfaces and chargers. LXT covers the vast majority of Makita's cordless range, while XGT targets the most demanding industrial work. US buyers should decide which platform their fleet will be built on before investing in batteries.

faq.q: What warranty does Makita offer in the US?
faq.a: Makita's standard US power tool warranty is a three-year limited warranty covering the tool, battery, and charger on most cordless products. That is shorter than some competitors offer, though Makita tools are generally regarded as durable. Always confirm warranty terms on the specific model and kit, as coverage can vary by product line.
